findings.text: Simulation domain context aggregates deferred handling state: a work item for later dispatch, a count of simulated lines, shared pending storage, linkage to owning domain, a record of optional callbacks, and opaque caller data.
Per line simulation context holds a boolean enabled marker plus a back pointer to the shared domain context, allowing mask state and pending storage to be reached from chip data.
Masking and unmasking only flip the per line enabled marker retrieved through chip data; no hardware access or pending change is shown on those paths.

Type configuration accepts only combinations of rising and falling edge selections and rejects any other trigger bits with an invalid argument failure; accepted values are recorded as the trigger type.

Pending query and pending update support only the pending state and are gated on the enabled marker. Query reports the shared pending bit. Update writes that bit and, when asserting, schedules the shared deferred work. Other states fail as invalid.

Resource acquire and release hooks forward to optional caller callbacks with domain, hardware number and caller data when present; acquire returns the callback result while release ignores results, and both succeed silently when no callback is installed.
Simulation chip object wires mask, unmask, type, pending query, pending update, and resource hooks together under one controller identity for use by mapped lines.

Deferred simulation handler repeatedly locates the next set pending bit, clears it, translates the hardware offset through the domain mapping, and invokes simple dispatch on the resolved descriptor until no pending bits remain.

Domain map allocates a per line context, installs the simulation chip and chip data, selects simple dispatch, adjusts request and probe related status, and links the shared context. Unmap clears dispatch, resets hardware number and chip linkage, and frees the per line context.

Simulation domain creation allocates a zeroed shared context and zeroed pending storage, creates a linear domain bound to that context, initializes count and hard deferred work and caller data, optionally copies caller callbacks, and transfers ownership of allocations to the domain. A simpler wrapper passes no callbacks or data.
Simulation domain removal first synchronizes outstanding deferred work, then releases pending storage and shared context, and finally removes the domain itself.

Managed variants create a simulation domain and register an automatic cleanup action that invokes ordinary removal; creation failure propagates the domain error and action registration failure propagates its error after reset.

Test fake controller groups no operation lifecycle hooks with an affinity hook that records effective affinity and a startup hook reporting success, marked to skip wake handling. A trivial handler reports handled.
Fake test setup allocates one descriptor, installs the fake controller with simple dispatch, clears the no request restriction, and returns the allocated virtual number.

Depth tests specify a counter discipline: zero after successful request, incremented by disable, decremented by enable, preserved across free while disabled and reset by a later request, preserved across managed shutdown and reactivation and across CPU offline and online transitions, with activation and managed affinity markers checked around those transitions.

Early interrupt bring up initializes default affinity, queries architecture for preallocated count, clamps total and preallocated counts to sparse limits, reconciles totals, inserts preallocated descriptors or initializes a static descriptor table with bad dispatch and depth one, then hands control to architecture early setup.

Sparse descriptor storage is protected by an external mutex and RCU aware tree configuration. Lookup at or after an offset requires RCU read context and is bounded by total count. Filesystem initialization holds the mutex while creating the base object and adding existing descriptors.

Per descriptor raw spinlock with interrupt exclusion guards reads of controller name, hardware number, level versus edge classification, wakeup marking, assigned name, and action list. One redirect path dispatches through container linkage to the owning descriptor.

Interrupt filesystem exposure offers seven read only attributes covering per CPU counts, chip name, hardware number, type, wakeup, name, and actions. Release frees mask storage, per CPU statistics, and the descriptor; a deferred RCU callback drops the final object reference.

Generic dispatch helpers resolve a virtual number or a domain plus hardware number to a descriptor and invoke descriptor handling. Safe forms preserve interrupt state around dispatch. The NMI form asserts NMI context before dispatch.

Teardown must synchronize deferred simulation work before releasing pending storage and context, otherwise the drain loop could access freed memory. Unmap must not run concurrently with dispatch that still resolves the same virtual number.

No locking is visible around the per line enabled marker or around pending bit test and update versus the drain loop, so concurrent mask and state operations may race unless callers serialize them externally.
Simulation controller advertises identity irq_sim.
Test controller advertises identity fake and test suite advertises identity irq_test_cases.
